It would be great if OpenCode core could add a similar mechanism — for example, a lightweight post-step hook that reminds the model to sync todo status, or automatically transitions stale `in_progress` items based on tool execution context. ## Update: SQLite contention is NOT the only cause — also reproduces with no other opencode process running

After filing this issue I tested again under different conditions and found this **also reproduces with zero other `opencode` processes running on the system**. So my SQLite-contention root cause is incomplete — it's a real symptom and a real failure mode, but it's not the only one.

### New repro (today, 2026-05-14 19:06:51)

Killed all `opencode` processes (verified with `ps -ef | grep opencode` returning nothing). Launched OpenCode Desktop fresh. Sidecar started cleanly, server ready at `http://127.0.0.1:63572`. **67 seconds later** the sidecar exited with `code: 1`. Same silent death pattern, no stderr.

```
[19:06:54.196] [info]  spawning sidecar { url: 'http://127.0.0.1:63572' }
[19:06:55.611] [info]  server ready { url: 'http://127.0.0.1:63572' }
[19:07:00.924] [info]  no update available
[19:08:02.016] [warn]  sidecar exited { code: 1 }   <-- no stderr between server-ready and exit
```

`log show --predicate 'eventMessage CONTAINS "192644 of"' --start "2026-05-14 19:00:00" --end "2026-05-14 19:09:00" | wc -l` returns **0** for that window. No SQLITE_MISUSE this time.

### What's likely actually happening

`runningboardd` shows that at the EXACT millisecond of sidecar death, **9 child `node` processes also terminated via `proc_exit`**:

```
2026-05-14 19:08:02.050 [com.apple.runningboard:process] [anon<node>(501):50483] termination reported by proc_exit
2026-05-14 19:08:02.050 [com.apple.runningboard:process] [anon<node>(501):50025] termination reported by proc_exit
2026-05-14 19:08:02.050 [com.apple.runningboard:process] [anon<node>(501):50484] termination reported by proc_exit
2026-05-14 19:08:02.050 [com.apple.runningboard:process] [anon<node>(501):50044] termination reported by proc_exit
2026-05-14 19:08:02.051 [com.apple.runningboard:process] [anon<node>(501):50045] termination reported by proc_exit
2026-05-14 19:08:02.051 [com.apple.runningboard:process] [anon<node>(501):50221] termination reported by proc_exit
2026-05-14 19:08:02.052 [com.apple.runningboard:process] [anon<node>(501):49903] termination reported by proc_exit
2026-05-14 19:08:02.052 [com.apple.runningboard:process] [anon<node>(501):49957] termination reported by proc_exit
2026-05-14 19:08:02.052 [com.apple.runningboard:process] [anon<node>(501):49902] termination reported by proc_exit
```

All 9 are `/Users/ottosulin/.nvm/versions/node/v20.19.2/bin/node` — these are MCP server children spawned by the sidecar. My `opencode.json` configures these MCP servers (relevant entries):

```jsonc
"mcp": {
  "memory":     { "type": "local", "command": ["npx", "-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-memory"], ... },
  "playwright": { "type": "local", "command": ["npx", "@playwright/mcp@latest", "--extension"], ... }
}
```

The first 7 MCP node children spawned 3–5 seconds after sidecar start. The last 2 (PIDs 50483, 50484) spawned at `19:07:50.448` and `19:07:50.454` — **12 seconds before sidecar death**. This timing strongly suggests an MCP-server-side error propagated up and crashed the sidecar.

### Suspect: `@playwright/mcp@latest --extension` mode

I'm running `@playwright/mcp` v0.0.75 (latest as of repro), which ships an alpha playwright-core (`1.61.0-alpha-1778188671000`). Looking at upstream playwright-mcp release notes, **the `--extension` code path has been actively bug-fixed in the last three releases**:

- **v0.0.75 (May 7)**: "Serialize shared browser launch in `--isolated` mode", "**Forward browser-level CDP commands in extension mode**" — directly touches `--extension`
- **v0.0.74 (May 6)**: "**Auto-recover when the remote browser disconnects mid-session**", "**Recover from page renderer crash**" — without these fixes, MCP server would crash on disconnect/renderer-crash
- **v0.0.72 (Apr 30)**: "**Surface unhandled rejections in `browser_run_code_unsafe` instead of crashing the server**" — direct admission that previous versions crashed the MCP

I ran into a very concrete version of this problem with the built-in Gemini/Google provider.

After connecting a valid `GOOGLE_API_KEY`, OpenCode still shows many models in `/models` that are either:
- not actually available to the current API key/account,
- not intended for normal chat/coding use,
- or simply not models I want to keep in the picker.

The current workaround is to:
1. disable the built-in `gemini` provider,
2. create a custom provider,
3. manually re-list only the allowed models.

That workaround is functional, but it has two downsides:
- it is much more cumbersome than `/connect`,
- and it loses the benefits of built-in provider metadata unless everything is re-declared manually (for example model capability/limit metadata).

A very helpful improvement would be:
- after `/connect` succeeds, allow the user to optionally customize the model list for that connected provider,
- ideally as an allowlist / "keep these models" step,
- and persist that selection so hidden models do not appear in `/models` or model pickers.

This would solve the common "connected provider but noisy/unusable model list" problem without forcing users into custom provider config just to hide models.

In other words: `/connect` should support a user-curated model list for built-in providers.

**Update: Root cause found. This was not an SSE parser issue.**

After extensive debugging, the actual root cause was a **provider SDK configuration mismatch**.

**The problem:** My Baseten provider config had `"npm": "@ai-sdk/openai"` instead of the correct `"npm": "@ai-sdk/baseten"`. The `@ai-sdk/openai` SDK sends requests in OpenAIs format, which does not fully match Baseten streaming behavior for tool calls. This caused tool call argument chunks to be emitted incompletely (literally just `{` instead of full JSON), leading to `JSON Parse error` downstream.

**The fix:** Use the official `@ai-sdk/baseten` provider:
```json
"baseten": {
  "npm": "@ai-sdk/baseten",
  "name": "Baseten",
  "options": {
    "baseURL": "https://inference.baseten.co/v1",
    "apiKey": "<your-key>"
  }
}
```

**Key takeaway:** The SSE stream parser and eventsource-parser were working correctly the entire time. The malformed data was already in the stream because the wrong SDK was negotiating the request format. If you are using Baseten with custom models, make sure your config uses `@ai-sdk/baseten`, not `@ai-sdk/openai` or `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`.

## Update: root cause found

Further testing shows the issue is broader than just `--`. Even `"chezmoi *": "ask"` and `"chezmoi git *": "ask"` fail to block `chezmoi git -- push`.

This appears to be the same root cause as the closed issue #6676 — the bash tool uses treesitter to tokenize commands before permission matching, and skips certain node types. The `--` token is stripped during tokenization, so `chezmoi git -- push` is evaluated as if it were `chezmoi git push`.

**Confirming the treesitter theory:** the pattern `"chezmoi git push": "ask"` (without `--`) **does** block `chezmoi git -- push`. This confirms `--` is being dropped before pattern matching occurs.

So #6676 was closed but the fix was incomplete — it only addressed the `kill -9` style flags, not `--` argument separators.

# Production Review: fix(tui): insert skill name without wiping existing prompt text

## Change Summary

A 3-line change to the `DialogSkill` `onSelect` handler in `packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/tui/component/prompt/index.tsx`:

```diff
-                input.setText(`/${skill} `)
-                setStore("prompt", {
-                  input: `/${skill} `,
-                  parts: [],
-                })
-                input.gotoBufferEnd()
+                input.insertText(`/${skill} `)
+                setStore("prompt", "input", input.plainText)
+                syncExtmarksWithPromptParts()
```

## What Changed

1. **`input.setText()` → `input.insertText()`**: Instead of destructively replacing the entire prompt, the skill name is inserted at the current cursor position, preserving existing text.

2. **`setStore("prompt", { input, parts: [] })` → `setStore("prompt", "input", input.plainText)`**: Instead of resetting the entire `prompt` store (which wipes `parts`), only the `input` field is updated to reflect the new combined text.

3. **`input.gotoBufferEnd()` → `syncExtmarksWithPromptParts()`**: Instead of moving the cursor to the end, the extmarks (virtual text positions for files/agents/paste) are re-synced with the prompt parts. This is consistent with how `onContentChange` already handles state sync.

## Review Checklist

### Correctness
- [x] `input.insertText()` is the established pattern used throughout this file (history restore, paste, file attachments, `PromptAppend` event handler)
- [x] `syncExtmarksWithPromptParts()` is already called in `onContentChange` and IME submission sync — consistent usage
- [x] `setStore("prompt", "input", rawText)` matches how `onContentChange` syncs state
- [x] No new imports needed — all APIs are already imported

### Edge Cases
- [x] **Empty input**: Works fine — `insertText` adds the skill name, `plainText` returns the combined text
- [x] **Multi-line input**: Cursor stays at the insertion point; extmarks are re-synced by position
- [x] **Existing extmarks (files, pastes)**: `syncExtmarksWithPromptParts()` preserves them as `onContentChange` does
- [x] **IME composition**: Not affected — the dialog is a modal popup, so IME is not active during skill selection

### Risk Assessment
- **Risk**: Very low. This is a 3-line change using only existing APIs.
- **Tests**: No test changes needed — this is purely a UI interaction change.
- **Rollback**: Trivial — revert the 3 lines.

## Issues

⚠️ **The PR diff is noisy** — the HaleTom fork's `dev` branch is significantly behind upstream `anomalyco/dev`. The PR shows 1000+ lines of unrelated diffs from commands/system/workspace changes that are already in upstream dev. Only the 3-line hunk for `DialogSkill.onSelect` is relevant.

This won't prevent merging since GitHub will handle the diff correctly against the base branch, but it makes review harder to skim.

## Recommendation

✅ **Approve**. The change is correct, minimal, and uses established patterns. Please squash-merge to clean up the noisy diff.

## Testing results

Reproduced with a custom theme using `"background": "none"` (transparent). Built and tested from source with the fix.

### Before (unmodified source)
`borderColor={theme.background}` where `background` is `"none"` → resolves to `RGBA(0,0,0,0)` → renderer drops alpha → `┃` renders as pure black (`#000000`).

### After (with fix)
`borderColor={theme.backgroundPanel}` → `┃` renders in the `backgroundPanel` color (verified as `#2D292D` for the test pywal theme).

### Remaining limitation
The `┃` character is still a visible solid-color strip against a transparent terminal background because `borderColor\> controls the character's foreground, and the OpenTUI renderer doesn't handle alpha on character foregrounds. Full transparency would require either:
- Renderer-level alpha support for character foregrounds
- Or a `borderBackgroundColor` prop to make the border cell share the block's panel background
